To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presented methodology can be applied to improve retrieval quality for airborne as well as satellite-borne infrared limb sounders.

(i) the proposed method can improve the retrieval quality for airborne infrared limb sounder measurements, (ii) it can be applied to other instruments including satellite-borne nadirsounders and near future satellite-borne limb instruments, (iii) it exploits the fact that neighbouring profiles are similar to one another, (iv) it produces 2-D cross sections instead of 1-D profiles and (v) the 2-D cross section retrieval produces typical diagnostic quantities.
the retrieval quality of modern airborne infrared limb sounder data can be improved by horizontal regularization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the retrieval of large-scale 2-D cross-sectional structures from limb-sounder data.
improving the retrieval quality of airborne limb sounders.
the retrieval of atmospheric profiles of temperature and trace gas mixing ratios from high-resolution limb-sounding measurements of atmospheric infrared emission spectra.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
horizontal regularisation can be used to improve the retrieval quality for all types of sounders that produce a large number of profiles in a short time.
the presented approach can improve the quality of limb-sounder data and that this improvement will become even more important for the next generation of satellite-borne sounders.
the presented approach has the potential to significantly improve the retrieval quality for airborne and satellite-borne limb and nadir sounders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
horizontal regularisation is a powerful technique to improve retrieval quality.
the presented method can be applied to improve retrieval quality and that it is a promising tool for the analysis and interpretation of large data sets.
the retrieval of 2-D crosssections instead of 1-D profiles is a viable alternative that should be considered when designing future limb sounders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the retrieval of 2-D cross sections is a promising way to improve the retrieval quality for limb sounders.
it is beneficial to exploit the spatial coherence of neighbouring measurements for limb sounders.
the retrieval quality of airborne infrared limb sounder data can be improved substantially by exploiting the high temporal resolution of the measurements.
